history.period: 1661 CE (1583 Saka), built during the reign of Maharaja Govinda Manikya with the help of his younger brother
history.summary: CSV town 'Udaipur' is CORRECT - but this is NOT the 19th-century Radha Kishore Manikya Jagannath temple of Agartala (Ujjayanta Palace grounds, 19th c., octagonal base, bright orange shikharas): that temple stands in AGARTALA, and any brief locating it at Udaipur is a conflation. It is also NOT the Puri Jagannath temple. The Udaipur row refers to the old 17th-century stone Jagannath temple on the SOUTHWEST BANK OF JAGANNATHDIGHI at Udaipur, built entirely of stone in 1661 CE (1583 Saka) during the reign of Maharaja Govinda Manikya with the help of his younger brother. Square in plan with corner buttresses, plain exterior walls with niches (the images are now empty); ASI's 'Temples of Tripura' calls it 'the most important of all the temples of Tripura'. A Vishnu image and an Uma-Maheshvara image were discovered nearby. Jagannath Dighi itself is an old royal tank at Udaipur whose waterfront was developed and inaugurated by CM Manik Saha in Feb 2024. MEDIA FLAG: no reliable image of this specific old Udaipur stone temple was found after genuine searching - image results for 'Jagannath temple Tripura' show the Agartala temple or Puri; media is left empty rather than risk a misattributed photo. Coordinates are from a Udaipur map listing ('Jagannath Temple', Matarbari/Udaipur) and are approximate - verify.

name: Jagannath Temple
town: Udaipur (southwest bank of Jagannath Dighi, Udaipur town)
town_description: Udaipur, in Gomati district on the Gomati river about 55 km from Agartala, was the capital of the Tripura kingdom under the Manikya dynasty before the capital shifted to Agartala. It is a cluster of 16th-17th century Manikya temples: the Shakti Peetha of Tripura Sundari at Matabari, the Bhuvaneswari temple by the Gomati, the Gunabati group of brick temples, and the old stone Jagannath temple by Jagannath Dighi.
